newsitem.title: USA: Clinton calls for tax incentives for US capital.
newsitem.headline: Clinton calls for tax incentives for US capital.

text.p: President Clinton on Tuesday called for stepped-up efforts to revitalize poor urban and rural neighborhoods, including private-sector tax incentives to bolster the U.S. capital city.

"We must pledge tonight that we will use this empowerment approach -- including private-sector tax incentives -- to renew our capital city, so that Washington is a great place to live and work," Clinton said.

In a prepared text of his State of the Union address, Clinton called for a doubling in the number of so-called empowerment zones around the country, a restoration of contaminated urban land and buildings to productive use and an expansion of the network of community development banks.
"We must do more ... to create jobs through investment by business and loans by banks," he said.
Clinton also set a target of 500 toxic waste sites to be cleaned up in coming years, double the 250 that were cleaned up in the last four years.
"Big polluters must live by this simple rule: if you pollute our environment, you pay to clean it up," he said.
